study_identification.title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantify deviations from the normative range of neuroanatomical variation in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P) and evaluate their overlap with healthy variation and their association with positive symptoms, cognition, and conversion to a psychotic disorder.

dataset_name.answer: ENIGMA Clinical High Risk for Psychosis Working Group

quality_checking_detail.answer: The ENIGMA Consortium quality assessment pipeline was used. Participants with <5% of missing regional measures or intracranial volume values per individual scan were considered high-quality.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Site harmonization was implemented using ComBat-GAM.

model_origin_detail.answer: The normative models for each regional measure in the framework were developed using data from an independent multisite sample of 37 407 healthy individuals (53.3% female; aged 3-90 years).

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness (CT), cortical surface area (SA), and subcortical volume (SV)

predictor_variables.answer: Age, Sex, Site, ICV, mean CT, mean SA

predictor_effects.answer: Fixed effects for age, sex, ICV, mean CT, and mean SA. Site was included as a covariate in the ComBat-GAM harmonization.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used ComBat-GAM for site harmonization and included covariates like ICV, mean CT, and mean SA in the models, which addresses nuisance variables.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Through this pipeline, we identified multivariable fractional polynomial regression as the optimal algorithm; the optimal covariate combination involved site harmonization (ComBat-GAM [combatting batch effects-generalized additive model]) and the inclusion of intracranial volume, mean CT, and mean SA in the models of the regional measures of SV, CT, and SA, respectively.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study used a pre-trained model, so there was no training within the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The normative models for each regional measure in the framework were developed using data from an independent multisite sample of 37 407 healthy individuals (53.3% female; aged 3-90 years).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The normative model was applied to the ENIGMA CHR-P sample, which is an independent dataset from the one used to train the model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The model parameters in the normative framework (CentileBrain) were then applied to each regional CT, SA, and SV measure of the individuals with CHR-P and healthy individuals in theENIGMAsample.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study did not validate the model on a different domain.

clinical_dataset.answer: ENIGMA Clinical High Risk for Psychosis Working Group

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear regression models were used to assess associations between positive symptoms and IQ with each regional z score and each ADS. Age was included as a variable in all regression models. Analyses were conducted with and without site as a random effect. The brain basis set (BBS) method was used to identify multivariate patterns of associations of regional z scores with IQ and positive symptoms.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Macroscale neuromorphometric measures may not provide an adequate explanation of psychosis risk.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Individuals with CHR-P and healthy individuals overlapped in the distributions of the observed values, regional z scores, and all ADS values. For any given region, the proportion of individuals with CHR-P who had infranormal or supranormal values was low and similar to that of healthy individuals. Individuals with CHR-P who converted to a psychotic disorder had a higher percentage of infranormal values in temporal regions compared with those who did not convert and healthy individuals. In the CHR-P group, only the ADS SA was associated with positive symptoms and IQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The data were collected at multiple sites using different scanners and protocols. Although site effects were accounted for, residual effects cannot be fully excluded. The neuroimaging data are cross-sectional and do not capture potential longitudinal changes.
